open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 scratch-limit outcome
open_points.text: the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see ... Outcomes are closed and checked in this order ... a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`
open_points.question: If agent code catches the over-limit file-write error and returns conforming outputs, how does the sandbox learn that the scratch limit was hit, and must the execution still be `resource_exhausted`?
options: The runner records every rejected over-limit write through a specified mechanism, so even a caught error yields `resource_exhausted`.
Only an uncaught write error or abnormal limit termination yields `resource_exhausted`; code that catches the error may succeed.
A caught over-limit write always becomes `crashed` rather than `resource_exhausted`.
open_points.default_guess: Classify an observable uncaught over-limit write as `resource_exhausted`, but allow an execution that catches the write error and returns valid outputs to succeed because no detection channel is specified.
